ai.literal: Than excessive anger, worse indeed is the forgetfulness in the elation of great joy.
ai.translation: Forgetfulness born of the elation of great joy is far worse than even excessive anger.
ai.modern: அளவுகடந்த கோபத்தை விட, மிகுந்த மகிழ்ச்சியினால் ஏற்படும் மனமகிழ்ச்சியில் வரும் மறதி (கடமை தவறுதல்) மிகவும் தீமையானது ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the danger of losing one's vigilance, or forgetfulness ('cōrvu'), when overwhelmed by extreme happiness. While excessive anger ('iṟanta vekuḷi') is known to cause immense harm, the author argues that the slackness or negligence that creeps in during moments of intense joy ('uvakai makiḻcci') is even more destructive. When a person is overjoyed, they let their guard down, making them highly vulnerable to errors and enemies. Therefore, maintaining constant watchfulness, even in moments of great celebration, is vital.

ai.literal: Forgetfulness destroys fame, in the manner that daily poverty destroys wisdom.
ai.translation: Just as constant poverty destroys one's wisdom, so does negligence destroy one's fame.
ai.modern: தினசரி வறுமையானது ஒருவனுடைய அறிவை அழிப்பதைப் போல, மறதி அல்லது அலட்சியம் ஒருவனுடைய புகழை அழித்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a powerful analogy to warn against negligence or forgetfulness (pocāppu). The poet compares the destructive power of negligence to that of constant, daily poverty (nicca nirappu). Just as relentless poverty wears down and ultimately destroys a person's wisdom and intellect (aṟivu), habitual carelessness or forgetfulness will ruin a person's hard-earned fame (pukaḻ). The word 'pocāppu' here denotes a state of mental slackness or lack of vigilance, which is shown to be fatal to one's reputation.

words.gloss: even to the authors of treatises

ai.literal: To those who are negligent there is no fame; that is the conclusion of the authors of treatises of whatever category in this world.
ai.translation: There is no greatness or fame for those who are negligent; this is the unanimous conclusion of the scholars of every kind of treatise in the world.
ai.modern: மறதி அல்லது சோம்பல் உடையவர்களுக்குப் புகழ் உண்டாவது இல்லை; அது உலகத்தில் உள்ள எந்த வகையான நூல்களை எழுதியவர்களுக்கும் துணிவான முடிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute incompatibility of negligence (பொச்சாப்பு) and fame (புகழ்மை). The author states that those who act with forgetfulness or lack of vigilance can never acquire greatness. To reinforce this truth, the couplet asserts that this is not just a personal opinion, but the settled conclusion (துணிவு) of scholars of all kinds of treatises (எப்பால் நூலோர்க்கும்) across the world. The word 'பொச்சாப்பு' refers to a state of self-forgetful carelessness, which destroys any chance of lasting achievement.

ai.literal: To those who have fear, there is no fortress; likewise, there is no good to those who have forgetfulness.
ai.translation: Just as there is no fortress that can protect those who are fearful, there is no good that can come to those who are negligent.
ai.modern: அச்சம் உடையவர்களுக்குப் பாதுகாப்புத் தரும் அரண் என்று எதுவும் இல்லை; அதுபோல, மறதியும் அலட்சியமும் உடையவர்களுக்கு எந்த நன்மையும் உண்டாவதில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a powerful analogy to warn against negligence or forgetfulness (பொச்சாப்பு). A person who is constantly gripped by fear cannot find safety even within a mighty fortress, because their own mind defeats them. Similarly, a person who is careless and forgetful can never achieve any lasting good or success, regardless of their opportunities. The poet emphasizes that internal discipline and alertness are far more critical than external circumstances.

ai.literal: Beforehand without guarding, he who neglected, his own mistake, afterwards [when] harm [comes], having regretted, will end up.
ai.translation: One who fails to guard himself beforehand and acts with negligence will surely end up lamenting his mistake later when ruin strikes.
ai.modern: முன்கூட்டியே தன்னைக் காத்துக் கொள்ளாமல் சோம்பலால் தவறியவன், பின்னர் துன்பம் வரும்போது தன் பிழையை நினைத்து வருந்துவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the danger of negligence and the importance of foresight. The word 'முன்னுற' means 'beforehand', emphasizing that precautions must be taken before danger arrives. 'இழுக்கியான்' refers to a person who slips or fails due to forgetfulness or carelessness. When such a person does not guard themselves in advance, they will inevitably face harm ('ஊறு') later. At that point, they can only lament their own mistake ('தன்பிழை'), but it will be too late to avert the consequences.

ai.literal: Unforgetfulness towards anyone at all times, without failing if it is obtained, that equal there is none.
ai.translation: If one can practice constant vigilance towards everyone at all times without fail, there is nothing else equal to that virtue.
ai.modern: எல்லோரிடத்திலும் எப்போதும் மறதி இல்லாமல் விழிப்புடன் இருக்கும் குணம் ஒருவருக்குத் தவறாமல் அமையுமானால், அதற்கு இணையானது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of constant vigilance or non-forgetfulness (இழுக்காமை). The poet emphasizes that this quality must be maintained towards everyone (யார்மாட்டும்), regardless of their status, and at all times (என்றும்), rather than just during critical moments. The phrase 'வழுக்காமை வாயின்' means that if this state of mindfulness is achieved without any lapse or slip, it becomes an incomparable asset. The couplet concludes that there is absolutely nothing equal (அதுவொப்பது இல்) to such unwavering, universal attentiveness.

ai.literal: Difficult things, saying [thus], impossible there is not, if one does, guarding with the unforgetting instrument.
ai.translation: There is nothing that is impossible, dismissed as too difficult, if one performs actions with care, using the instrument of unforgetfulness.
ai.modern: மறதி இல்லாத மனமாகிய கருவியைக் கொண்டு, எச்சரிக்கையுடன் ஒரு செயலைச் செய்தால், 'இது செய்வதற்கு அரியது' என்று முடியாத காரியம் எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of constant vigilance and mindfulness in achieving any goal. The poet states that no task is impossible or too difficult to accomplish if it is undertaken with an unforgetting mind (பொச்சாவாக் கருவி) and guarded care (போற்றி). The 'unforgetting instrument' refers to a mind that is always alert, focused, and free from negligence. By maintaining this state of active awareness, even the most challenging obstacles can be overcome, leaving nothing as truly impossible.

words.gloss: those things praised by the wise

ai.literal: Those things praised, guarding and doing is required; without doing, to those who neglected, even in seven births there is none.
ai.translation: One must cherish and perform those actions praised by the wise; for those who neglect them and fail to perform them, there is no redemption even in seven births.
ai.modern: சான்றோரால் புகழப்பட்ட செயல்களைப் போற்றிச் செய்ய வேண்டும்; அவற்றைச் செய்யாமல் அலட்சியம் செய்தவர்க்கு ஏழு பிறவிகளிலும் நன்மை உண்டாகாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the severe consequences of negligence or forgetfulness in performing one's duties. The poet advises that we must carefully guard and perform those noble deeds that have been praised (புகழ்ந்தவை) by wise elders. If a person neglects (செய்யாது இகழ்ந்தார்க்கு) these duties out of laziness or carelessness, they will suffer the consequences. The phrase 'எழுமையும் இல்' warns that such negligent individuals will find no happiness or elevation in any of their seven successive births.

ai.literal: Those who were ruined because of negligence, let them think of, when they themselves experience infatuation because of their own joy.
ai.translation: Let people think of those who were ruined by negligence, at the very moment they find themselves infatuated with their own joy.
ai.modern: தங்கள் மகிழ்ச்சியினால் செருக்குற்று மயங்கும் காலத்தில், மறதியினால் (அலட்சியத்தினால்) அழிந்து போனவர்களை நினைத்துப் பார்க்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the danger of complacency that arises from excessive happiness or success. When people are overjoyed, they often lose their vigilance and become infatuated or prideful ('மைந்துறும்'). To prevent the ruin that follows such negligence ('இகழ்ச்சி'), the poet advises them to remember those who were once prosperous but got ruined because they let their guard down. Reflecting on the downfall of others serves as a powerful reality check to maintain mindfulness.

ai.literal: That which was intended to attain is easy indeed, if one is able to keep in mind that very thing which was intended.
ai.translation: It is easy to attain what one has planned, if one can keep that very plan constantly in mind without forgetfulness.
ai.modern: நினைத்ததை அடைவது மிகவும் எளிது, நினைத்த காரியத்தையே எப்போதும் மறவாமல் நினைவில் வைத்திருக்க முடிந்தால்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the power of constant focus and mindfulness in achieving success. The poet asserts that achieving a goal is highly feasible, provided one does not lose sight of the initial intention. The repetition of the word 'உள்ளியது' (that which was thought) emphasizes that the key to success lies in keeping the original objective continuously in one's thoughts. By avoiding forgetfulness and maintaining unwavering attention, any intended outcome becomes easily attainable.
